text:
noah: hey team, new hire on Ubuntu 22.04. WireGuard newhire-prod shows as connected but I can't ssh to bastion or curl internal api (api.internal.redwood.internal). `dig api.internal.redwood.internal @10.10.0.53` returns the IP, but `curl` times out. Any ideas? :confused:

it-ops: welcome! quick thought: systemd-resolved on Ubuntu uses 127.0.0.53 stub resolver. split-tunnel WireGuard might not be registering per-link DNS with systemd, so look at `resolvectl status` and the wg0 link. Can you paste `resolvectl status wg0` and `ip route`?

noah: here are snippets:```
$ resolvectl status wg0
Link 5 (wg0)
      Current Scopes: DNS
      LLMNR setting: no
      MulticastDNS setting: no
      DNSSEC setting: no
      DNSSEC supported: no
      DNS Servers: 10.10.0.53
      DNS Domain: ~redwood.internal
$ ip route show
10.10.0.0/16 dev wg0 proto kernel scope link
default via 192.168.1.1 dev wlp3s0 proto dhcp metric 600
```
Weirdly `resolvectl query api.internal.redwood.internal` returns the IP but `curl --resolve "api.internal.redwood.internal:443:10.10.4.12" https://api.internal.redwood.internal/health` also times out. SSH to bastion `ssh -vv bastion` shows TCP handshake hanging.

rachel: that points to routing rather than DNS. Can you `sudo ss -tna | grep 443` while reproducing the curl to watch SYN states? Also check `sudo iptables -L -n` (or nft) in case local firewall is blocking wg0 forwarding. On laptops we sometimes have nftables configured by `ufw` blocking forwarded traffic for non-root processes.

noah: `ss` shows lots of SYN-SENT to the internal IP and no SYN-RECV. `sudo ufw status` shows "Status: active" and default incoming deny, but there are allowed rules for OpenSSH only. Hmm.

it-ops: ok, UFW default drop on incoming can still block forwarded traffic if FORWARD policy is set to DROP. Check `sudo ufw show raw` to see underlying iptables rules. For a quick test, try `sudo ufw disable` then attempt `curl`/`ssh` again. If that fixes it, add a rule: `sudo ufw allow in on wg0` and `sudo ufw allow out on wg0` or set `ufw route allow in on wg0 to any` depending on your ufw version.

noah: disabled ufw, retried and SSH/connect works immediately. ok that was it. I re-enabled ufw and ran:```
sudo ufw allow in on wg0 to any
sudo ufw allow out on wg0 from any
```
then reload and confirmed connections succeed.

rachel: nice find. We'll add a note to the onboarding doc: for Linux hosts using ufw/nftables, allow wg interface traffic or use a post-up hook in WireGuard to adjust firewall rules. Example post-up snippet for /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf:```
PostUp = /usr/sbin/ufw route allow in on wg0 && /usr/sbin/ufw route allow out on wg0
PostDown = /usr/sbin/ufw route delete allow in on wg0 || true && /usr/sbin/ufw route delete allow out on wg0 || true
```
Also mention systemd-resolved per-link DNS if people hit name resolution issues; you can use `resolvectl dns wg0 10.10.0.53` and `resolvectl domain wg0 ~redwood.internal` in PostUp as well.

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-3845 to add Linux/ufw + WireGuard troubleshooting tips to the onboarding guide and to include a PostUp example for managed images.

noah: thanks everyone! leaving a tiny shell snippet here that helped me test quickly:```
# test DNS and connectivity without changing system config
resolvectl query api.internal.redwood.internal @10.10.0.53 && nc -vz 10.10.4.12 443
```
Saved my first-day sanity. :relieved:
